segments: 312 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And the Frankish infantry who were not able to flee
to a large, ruined fortress called Kokhba,
they set their sights on climbing up.
And the common people were left begging for mercy,
and like fire in stubble the sword of the Turks held sway among them.
And when the Turks relented from the slaughter,
they stripped those who remained of their shoes and their clothes;
and while men and women were naked, they bound them with ropes,
and compelled them to run alongside the horses.
Now the total number of the slain on the first occasion and this second one amounted to thirty thousand,
and sixteen thousand were carried off into captivity.
And those who escaped with the Frankish infantry into that ruined fortress were a thousand men.
Now not a single woman or child was saved,
except that those who did not perish
were sold into slavery in foreign regions.
And Edessa was left desolate,
and steeped in blood,
and full of the corpses of her sons and daughters.
And hyenas entered it by night to feed on the flesh of the slain,
and it became a dwelling for jackals.
Of Baldwin, the lord of Kaysum, not even his corpse was found;
and Joscelin secretly escaped to Samosata.
And our Bishop Basil was saved by flight,
while the bishop of the Armenians was captured along with many others.
Now the inner Franks,
when they heard of the calamity that had happened in Edessa,
were stirred up, and burst forth and went out from Italy, vast forces:
the king of Germany with ninety thousand horsemen,
and the king of France,
whom the Arabs call Louis,
with fifty thousand,
and infantry without number.
And in the year 1459
of the Greeks [1148 AD], they fought a battle with Constantinople,
because they knew the deceit of the Greeks.
However, King Manuel,
after the great amount of gold that he gave them,
swore that he would guide them without deceit.
Yet he immediately deceived them,
for he sent guides ahead of them who led them into rugged mountains without water.
And when they had spent five days wandering about,
and their guides had fled,
myriads of them died of thirst,
both they and their mounts.
And the Turks heard of it,
and fell upon the Franks, who were scattered ... the king of France:
